attributes.action: Provide funding to extend free Bee Network bus travel to all children aged 5–10
attributes.additional_details: The plan to introduce free Bee Network travel for 11–16s from January 2027 excludes children aged 5–10. This financially penalises families with younger children facing identical cost-of-living pressures, costing them up to £500 a year per child. Differentiating travel rights strictly based on age within compulsory education is unfair. The Government should provide funding to cover all children under 16, offering comprehensive relief to households and encouraging green travel habits early.Once
attributes.background: Fund the extension of free travel on Greater Manchester’s Bee Network to children aged 5–10. The current plan only covers 11–16s from January 2027. The Government must provide central funding to include primary-aged children, ensuring an equal and fair transport system for all families.

rejection.details: Funding and decisions for free travel schemes on Greater Manchester's Bee Network are decided by the Mayor of Greater Manchester and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA).
